\begin{definition}[Statistical distance]
\lean{TCSlib.InformationTheory.statDist}
\statementsource{Vad12}{
  pdf-bf2ce5422088-p172-b002,
  pdf-bf2ce5422088-p216-b003
}
\statementsource{HILL99}{pdf-130039751e9f-p007-b003}
\statementsource{raoyehudayoff-ch06-information}{pdf-6d7577246334-p003-b003}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p014-b013,

\label{TCSlib.InformationTheory.statDist}
\leanok
\uses{TCSlib.InformationTheory.FinDist}
Let $\alpha$ be a finite set, and let $p$ and $q$ be probability distributions on
$\alpha$. Their statistical distance is $\frac12\sum_{a\in\alpha}|p(a)-q(a)|$.
\end{definition}

  {pdf-70350d84fb7f-p002-b003}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set, and let $p$, $q$, and $r$ be probability distributions on
$\Omega$. Then $d_{\mathrm{stat}}(p,r)\le
d_{\mathrm{stat}}(p,q)+d_{\mathrm{stat}}(q,r)$.
\end{theorem}
